claim: A component that reads one field re-renders when that field changes and at no other time.
watch: Type in name: its counter climbs and billing's stays at 1; delete down past three characters to see the message.

claim: A rule that spans two fields reports against the path it names, so the message lands on shipping even though billing is the field being typed in.
watch: Change a digit in the billing postcode — the error appears under shipping, the field you never touched.

claim: Remove a row and every row below it keeps its own value, its own error and its own React key — only the addresses renumber.
watch: Add a line and leave it blank — it reads Required straight away. Give the two rows above it different skus, then remove the top row: every survivor keeps its value, the blank one keeps its Required, and the key printed beside each stays put while the address next to it shifts down.

claim: Two inputs on one form: useField keeps the value in React and re-renders on every keystroke, useUncontrolledField leaves it in the DOM node, so typing reaches React not at all.
watch: Type in the left box and its counter climbs by one on every keystroke; type in the right box and neither counter moves — then empty the right box, and "Required" appears beside it for the cost of a single render, which is the form saying it had every keystroke all along.

claim: A section switched off stops blocking submit and keeps every value typed into it, so the rules that read it go on reading it.
watch: Tick "same as billing": the error on the postcode clears and submit prints the payload it handed over — "shipping":{"postcode":"530-0002"} still in it — instead of "blocked by shipping.postcode"; untick and the rule judges whatever you typed while it was off.
